description: Wire the existing Treasury (internal/token/genesis.go) into the live node lifecycle and configuration so a running matrixd HONESTLY establishes native MATRIX supply on first start, and expose a funding operation reachable by operators/users so a buyer account can obtain MATRIX to spend. Then demonstrate the FULL economic loop on a live node with a real command transcript. This is the key gap: Treasury is fully tested but never constructed in node.go, so fresh accounts hold 0 MATRIX and the CLI loop cannot complete.
steps: In internal/node/node.go: after n.market and n.tokenChain are constructed in Start(), construct a token.Treasury via token.NewTreasury(n.market.Ledger(), n.kvStore) exactly as compute_settlement_test.go does. Store it on the Node struct and add a GetTreasury() accessor.

Extend node.Config with a Genesis section (yaml): a list of allocations (account ID -> amount in native base units) and a reward_pool amount. On Start(), call Treasury.ApplyGenesis(allocations, rewardPool) exactly once (it is idempotent via GenesisApplied() and persisted in the Pebble store), respecting NativeMaxSupply (1e18 base units). Log whether genesis was applied or already-applied. Do NOT double-credit on restart.

Update node.Initialize (matrixd --init) to write a sensible default Genesis section into config.yaml (e.g. a reward_pool seeded from the cap, and optional named allocations) so `matrixd --init` produces a config that yields a funded reward pool. Keep the default honest and under the cap.

Add a market gRPC funding RPC in proto/matrix/market/v1/market.proto: FundAccount(FundAccountRequest{account, amount}) returns (FundAccountResponse{account, balance}) that moves reward-pool MATRIX to an account through Treasury.FundFromRewardPool (never unlimited minting; respects cap; persisted). Add doc comments in the proto style used by the file. Run make proto (buf lint + buf generate must pass).

Implement FundAccount in internal/marketapi: the Service needs access to the Treasury. Extend marketapi.Config/NewServer/NewService to accept a funder (an interface with FundFromRewardPool(recipient string, amount uint64) error, satisfied by *token.Treasury) and wire it from node.go. Map token.ErrSupplyCapExceeded / market.ErrInsufficientFunds to appropriate gRPC codes (FailedPrecondition). Gate it behind the same ACL/auth as other mutating RPCs.

Add a `matrix fund` (or `matrix genesis fund`) CLI command in internal/cli that calls the FundAccount RPC: flags --account and --amount, prints the new balance. Wire it into NewRootCommand and add the market client method. Follow the existing job.go/balance.go command patterns.

Add unit tests: node-level test that ApplyGenesis runs once and is idempotent across a simulated restart (reuse the memBus/kv patterns from compute_settlement_test.go); marketapi integration test that FundAccount moves reward-pool funds and rejects over-cap/over-pool requests; a cli in-process test for the fund command against an in-memory MarketService (follow internal/cli/integration_test.go and root_test.go patterns).
Run make proto, go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./..., and go test -race on internal/node, internal/marketapi, internal/cli, internal/token.

DEMONSTRATE THE LIVE LOOP end to end and capture the real transcript into .agents/tasks/task-genesis-funding-quickstart/live-loop-transcript.txt: build matrixd + matrix; matrixd --init a temp config with a reward pool and ACLs disabled (dev) OR set MATRIX_ADMIN_API_KEY; start matrixd; use matrix to fund a buyer account from the reward pool; register a provider; submit a job; complete/settle it; and show `matrix balance` before/after proving native MATRIX actually moved buyer -> provider. If completing a job requires the buyer's signing key to settle through consensus, use the path the node actually supports (market CompleteJob direct ledger transfer for a single dev node, or the signed-transfer path) and document exactly which path was exercised.
acceptance_criteria: node.go constructs a token.Treasury and applies genesis exactly once on Start from config, idempotent across restart (verified by test), persisted in Pebble.

A funding path (market gRPC FundAccount + `matrix fund` CLI command) moves reward-pool MATRIX to an account through Treasury.FundFromRewardPool, respecting NativeMaxSupply and the pool balance; over-cap/over-pool requests are rejected with a clear error.
make proto, go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./... all pass; go test -race passes on touched packages.
A real transcript in live-loop-transcript.txt shows a live matrixd being funded, a provider registered, a job submitted and completed, and native MATRIX balances changing (buyer down, provider up).
verification: make proto && cd services/core && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...

Run the live loop: matrixd --init, start matrixd, matrix fund, matrix provider register, matrix job submit, matrix job complete, matrix balance (before/after) — capture transcript and confirm balances moved
findings:
Implemented and verified. Committed as ba82f7e (app/library code committed to main per orchestrator policy; .agents/ task metadata left untracked, matching the FEAT-001 commit convention).

WHAT CHANGED:
- node.go: added token.Treasury to the Node struct + GetTreasury() accessor; constructed it via token.NewTreasury(n.market.Ledger(), n.kvStore) right after market+tokenChain in Start(); apply genesis unconditionally on Start (ApplyGenesis is idempotent via the persisted GenesisApplied marker) and log applied-vs-already-applied. Added a Genesis section to node.Config (GenesisConfig{Allocations []{account,amount}, RewardPool uint64}). node.Initialize (matrixd --init) now writes a default genesis with reward_pool = token.NativeMaxSupply (1e18 base units == 1,000,000,000 whole MATRIX at the cap, no named allocations). Wired n.treasury as the marketapi Funder.
- proto/matrix/market/v1/market.proto: added FundAccount(FundAccountRequest{account,amount}) returns (FundAccountResponse{account,balance}) with doc comments; ran make proto (buf lint + buf generate) clean.
- marketapi: added a Funder interface {FundFromRewardPool(recipient string, amount uint64) error} (satisfied by *token.Treasury), threaded through Config/NewServer/NewService (funder is optional; FundAccount returns codes.Unimplemented when nil). Implemented FundAccount handler (validates account/amount, calls FundFromRewardPool, returns new ledger balance). Added token.ErrSupplyCapExceeded -> codes.FailedPrecondition in mapMarketError (market.ErrInsufficientFunds already mapped there, which covers over-pool funding). FundAccount is gated by the same auth interceptor as every other non-health RPC.
- cli: added `matrix fund --account --amount` (internal/cli/fund.go), wired into NewRootCommand; reuses printBalance. No client.go change needed (generated stub adds FundAccount to MarketServiceClient).

TESTS ADDED (all pass, incl. -race): internal/node/genesis_test.go (genesis applied once + idempotent across a reopened store simulating restart; default-config reward pool == NativeMaxSupply); internal/marketapi/fund_test.go (FundAccount moves pool funds and conserves supply, rejects over-pool with FailedPrecondition without moving funds, validates empty account / zero amount as InvalidArgument, Unimplemented without a funder); internal/cli/fund_test.go (in-process `matrix fund` funds a buyer and tops up, plus flag validation).

VERIFICATION RUN: make proto OK; go build ./... OK; go vet ./... OK; go test ./... all OK; go test -race ./internal/node/... ./internal/marketapi/... ./internal/cli/... ./internal/token/... all OK.

LIVE LOOP (real transcript at .agents/tasks/task-genesis-funding-quickstart/live-loop-transcript.txt): built matrixd + matrix, matrixd --init a temp config, started a single dev node with enable_acls=false. SETTLEMENT PATH EXERCISED: market CompleteJob = a direct market.Ledger transfer buyer -> provider (the sanctioned single-dev-node path; the consensus-backed node.ComputeSettlementCoordinator is the multi-node production default and is covered by compute_settlement_test.go, not by `matrix job complete`). BALANCE DELTAS observed (native base units): reward pool 1000000000000000000 -> 999999999999000000 after funding buyer 1,000,000; buyer-alice 0 -> 1,000,000 (funded) -> 999,950 (after settling a 10-unit @5 = 50 job); provider-bob 0 -> 50. Buyer down exactly 50, provider up exactly 50 => native MATRIX genuinely moved buyer -> provider.

GOTCHAS FOR LATER FEATURES:
1) node.Config network.listen_addr is fed straight to multiaddr; the plain 'host:port' form (including the default 0.0.0.0:9000) FAILS p2p host init ('/ip4/host:port/tcp/0' is invalid). Use a full multiaddr like /ip4/127.0.0.1/tcp/19000 for a live node. This is a PRE-EXISTING p2p/host.go quirk, not introduced here; consider fixing separately if a later feature needs matrixd to start from the default config.
2) The sandbox runs each execute_bash in its own PID namespace with --die-with-parent, so background processes do not survive across tool calls. The live loop had to be run as a single self-contained script (start node, run CLI loop, kill node) within one command; that script is preserved in git history intent but the temp build dir (.tmp-live) was removed after capturing the transcript.
3) FundFromRewardPool wraps the ledger Transfer error, but errors.Is still matches market.ErrInsufficientFunds, so over-pool requests map to FailedPrecondition as intended.
